_about: Every number here was measured by the code in this repo on the machine described in 'environment', except entries under 'published', which are quoted from other people's papers and tools for comparison. bpb = bits per byte of the original file. Lower is better.

environment.gpu: Intel Iris Xe integrated (unused - all inference on CPU)

published._source: xz/ts_zip figures from bellard.org/ts_zip; Hutter record from prize.hutter1.net; image/audio from arXiv:2309.10668

harness_validation._about: bench.py's own xz -9 measurement vs the published figure on the identical file. This is the check that makes every other number here credible.

classical_full_files._about: bench.py, whole files, round-trip verified per row.

ptc_evolution._about: Effect of adding a match model and a stride detector to the pure context-mixing compressor. Predicted in advance that kennedy.xls would gain most, because it is a fixed-record spreadsheet and the model was 1-D.

model_comparison._about: llm_ptc, identical 8192-byte sample of alice29.txt, identical coder, LIMIT=1024. Only the model changes.

headline_alice29._about: Full alice29.txt, 152089 bytes. llm_ptc rows are batched-encode MEASUREMENTS, not verified codec output - see caveats in the README.

contamination_test._about: Identical 50757-byte samples. post2026.txt is prose from a 2026 arXiv paper, published long after SmolLM2's training cutoff. xz is the control: it cannot memorise, so a surviving advantage over xz is not memorisation.

enwik8_ablation._about: 262144-byte slice from offset 50,000,000 of enwik8. Mid-file on purpose: the first 256 KB contains the XML preamble and scores an artificially good 0.811, a 13% bias.

variants.note: measured on the BIASED first-256KB slice, where LLM-only was 0.817

coder_efficiency._about: probe.py. 'raw model' is -log2 p under the model's own distribution; 'quantised' is under the 12-bit probabilities we actually code against; 'emitted' is real output. coder = emitted/quantised - 1. smoothing = quantised/raw - 1, where negative means the 12-bit clamp SMOOTHS an overconfident model and wins.

negative_results.claim: bfloat16 weights will be ~2x faster because the checkpoint is 16-bit and we are memory-bandwidth bound
negative_results.detail: 64 B/s vs float32's 84 B/s. No AVX512-BF16 on this CPU, so torch converts to fp32 per matmul and we pay conversion on top.

negative_results.claim: the gap to ts_zip is mostly our 512-token context resets
negative_results.detail: Sweeping context 256->1024 moved GPT-2's bpb by -0.7%, i.e. noise, and post-slide tokens cost the same as deep-in-window ones. The gap was the model.

negative_results.claim: blending a match prediction into the LLM distribution will help on repetitive markup
negative_results.detail: Naive linear interpolation measured 2% WORSE. Fixed by mixing in the logistic domain with learned weights, which then gave -1.2%.
It GAINS 5.3% against GPT-2 by smoothing an overconfident model. Against well-calibrated SmolLM2 it is worth +0.05%, i.e. nothing.

negative_results.claim: SSE/APM will help, as it does in every serious CM compressor
negative_results.detail: Neutral at 25% weight (0.918 vs 0.917), harmful at 75% (0.926). SSE fixes miscalibrated mixers; a well-calibrated LLM has nothing to recalibrate.

negative_results.claim: batched teacher-forced encoding is a free 16x speedup
negative_results.detail: 16x faster and byte-identical output, but the stream does NOT decode with the sequential decoder - diverged at byte 253. Valid as a ratio measurement, invalid as a codec until inference is integer.

negative_results.claim: the first 256 KB of enwik8 is a representative sample
negative_results.detail: 0.811 there vs 0.917 mid-file. The XML preamble inflated it by 13%.
